claims.statement: The filter is one recursive operator-discriminated grammar, MetadataPredicate<Condition>, instantiated for documents (MetadataFilter, fields are metadata keys) and for metadata entries (MetadataMatch, fields are key or value); parseMetadataFilter and parseMetadataMatch share one walker and differ only by record type.

The accepted operator set is and, or, not, eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, nin, all, contains, prefix, suffix, type, and exists; caseInsensitive is an optional flag rather than an operator, accepted only on string or string-array operands and rejected on exists and type.

parseMetadataFilter rejects unknown operators, unknown properties, missing required properties, and operator-incompatible values by throwing MetadataFilterError carrying the JSON path of the failing node.

METADATA_FILTER_LIMITS bounds untrusted filters at nesting depth 16, 256 nodes, 32 group operands, 64 membership values, a 128-byte field key limit, and a 1024-character string limit; exceeding a limit throws MetadataFilterError.
Entry matches accept only field key or value, and reject exists and all because they have no meaning for a single metadata entry; a number or boolean operand against the key field matches nothing.

Comparison, membership, and text conditions only compare against values of the operand's own type: a mismatch never matches, ordered operators reject boolean operands, and membership arrays must be non-empty, homogeneous, and are de-duplicated preserving order.

Array-valued metadata is treated as a set: a condition matches when any element satisfies it, all requires every listed value, and ne and nin require at least one same-type value under the key with no same-type value equal to the operand.
caseInsensitive folds ASCII letters only, on both the column and the operand, matching SQLite lower(); non-ASCII letters remain exact.
Filters compile to parameterized SQL in which every user key and value is a bound parameter; keys and values are never interpolated into SQL text.

The SQL compiler has two scopes: candidates compiles each condition to a correlated EXISTS probing a document's own rows, while corpus compiles each condition to an uncorrelated IN subquery evaluated once per statement, which discovery uses when counting documents.

Metadata is extracted only from the qmd.metadata mapping of a leading YAML frontmatter block in .md, .markdown, or .mdx files; extraction never throws, and files without frontmatter or the namespace yield empty metadata with no error.

Metadata extraction is all-or-nothing per document: invalid keys or values fail the whole document, which stores empty metadata with a bounded extraction error while the document still indexes normally.

Normalization rejects null values, empty arrays, nested arrays, mixed-type arrays, non-finite numbers, and control characters in keys, and enforces limits of 64 KiB frontmatter, 64 keys, 128-byte keys, 1024-character strings, 128-element arrays, and 100 YAML aliases.

Metadata is persisted in document_metadata keyed by document_id, recording extraction version, extraction error, and extraction time, plus document_metadata_values with one typed row per scalar keyed by document, key, and ordinal, with CHECK constraints enforcing exactly one typed column and partial indexes per value type.

replaceDocumentMetadata rewrites a document's metadata rows in one transaction, so a failed extraction clears stale metadata; a document is re-extracted through the full sync path whenever its file changes, and a METADATA_EXTRACTION_VERSION bump makes existing rows stale so qmd update re-extracts them.

Only active documents with a current-version extraction and no extraction error are eligible for filtered search and metadata discovery; documents outside that state are counted as pending by countDocumentsPendingMetadata and excluded from filter results.

The filter is applied inside each retrieval leg before RRF fusion and reranking: the FTS leg adds the compiled filter and the current, error-free extraction gate to its SQL, and the vector leg restricts scans to eligible rows, while metadata is attached to final results only after fusion and reranking.
A scoped or filtered FTS query materializes its match set with no inner LIMIT so the filter sees every match, while an unscoped query keeps the inner LIMIT for speed.

Every returned search result satisfies the filter, which is enforced in both the vector scan and again when vector rows resolve to documents, because a content hash can belong to both matching and non-matching documents.

Top-K completeness under highly selective filters is best-effort: the changelog states this, the hybrid pipeline seeds fusion with a top-20 FTS window, and vector candidate counts grow only while fewer than the requested documents resolve, up to the sqlite-vec cap.

listMetadata defaults to keyLimit 50, keyOffset 0, valueLimit 10, valueOffset 0, sort count, and minCount 1, and rejects out-of-domain options with MetadataOptionError that names the offending option.

A filter and a match together are checked against a budget of 30,000 SQL bindings before any statement is prepared, and exceeding it throws MetadataBindingBudgetError, because the match is bound twice.

In discovery, filter selects which documents are counted and sets filteredDocuments as the coverage denominator, while match selects which metadata entries are reported; counts are documents rather than values.

The discovery report is read inside one deferred transaction over one snapshot, and keys whose documents hold different types are split into per-type summaries with their own counts and ranges for numbers.
Every value reported by discovery under a given scope is reachable through an eq filter under the same scope.

The SDK validates every filter and match at its boundary with parseMetadataFilter and parseMetadataMatch before compiling SQL, and re-exports MetadataFilterError, MetadataOptionError, and MetadataBindingBudgetError.

The MCP metadata tool's match field is 'key' (the entry's key name) or 'value' (the entry's value), while its filter field names a metadata key of a document; invalid match, filter, or binding-budget errors return an isError tool result.
The MCP query tool validates filter with parseMetadataFilter and returns an isError tool result with the validator message when it is invalid.
HTTP POST /query and its alias POST /search return 400 for a non-object filter or an invalid filter AST, with the validator message in the error body.

HTTP POST /metadata returns 400 for invalid JSON, a non-object body, a non-object or invalid filter or match, an invalid sort, a non-array collections value, a non-numeric window option, and any MetadataOptionError or MetadataBindingBudgetError from the store.

The CLI qmd collection metadata command supports --filter, --match, and window and ordering flags, and rejects -n, --all, and structured output formats because it prints text only, pointing structured callers to the SDK, MCP metadata tool, or POST /metadata.
